title: नरसिंह अवतार महाकाव्यमा प्रयोगशीलता {Applicability in Narasimha Avatar epic}
nepali: यस लेखमा जगदीश शमशेर राणाद्वारा रचित नरसिंह अवतार महाकाव्यको प्रयोगवादी अवधारणाका आधारमा अध्ययन तथा विश्लेषण गरिएको छ । प्रयोगवाद आफैंमा कुनै वाद होइन, साहित्यमा गरिने नयाँ–नयाँ प्रयोगलाई प्रयोगवादी भन्ने चलन छ । नेपाली कवितामा प्रयोगवाद भन्नाले वि.सं. २०१७ सालको रूपरेखा पत्रिकामा प्रकाशित मोहन कोइरालाको घाइतेयुग कविताबाट सुरु भएको नयाँ कविता धारालाई बुझिन्छ । यस धाराका कवितामा अमूर्त लेखनशैली, सम्प्रेषणहीनता, संरचनागत शिथिलता, नयाँ नयाँ बिम्ब, प्रतीक र मिथकको प्रयोग, विसङ्गतिको प्रस्तुति र अस्तित्ववादी चेत जस्ता कुरा मुख्य विशेषताका रूपमा रहेका छन् । यिनै कुरालाई आधार बनाई यसमा नरसिंह अवतारको विषयवस्तु, कथानक, चरित्र, परिवेश, उद्देश्य, भाषाशैली आदि तत्वहरूको अध्ययन तथा विश्लेषण गरिएको छ । यस अध्ययनबाट प्रस्तुत महाकाव्य विषयवस्तुको छनोटमा, कथानक निर्माणमा, पात्रविधानमा, परिवेश निर्माणमा, उद्देश्यका साथै भाषाशैली आदिको प्रयोगमा परम्परित महाकाव्यक संरचना भन्दा भिन्न र नयाँढाँचाको प्रयोगशील बन्न पुगेको प्रस्ट भएको छ ।
american_english: This article presents a study and analysis of Jagadish Shamsher Rana's epic Narasimha Avatar on the basis of pragmatist concepts. Pragmatism is not itself an -ism; rather, there is a trend of calling new experiments in literature pragmatist. In Nepali poetry, pragmatism refers to the new poetry stream that began with Mohan Koirala's Ghayiteyuga poem, published in the outline pamphlet of 2017 BS. Poems of this stream are characterized mainly by abstract writing style, incommunicability, structural looseness, new images, use of symbols and myths, presentation of the absurd, and existential consciousness. On the basis of these elements, the subject matter, plot, character, setting, purpose, and language style of Narasimha Avatar have been studied and analyzed. From this study it is clear that, in the choice of subject matter, construction of plot, characterization, creation of setting, and use of language style and so on with purpose, this epic has become experimental with a new form rather than the conventional epic structure.

australian_english: This article studies and analyses Jagadish Shamsher Rana's epic Narasimha Avatar using pragmatist concepts as its basis. Pragmatism isn't an -ism in itself; rather, there's a trend in literature of calling new experiments pragmatist. In Nepali poetry, pragmatism means the new poetry stream that started with Mohan Koirala's Ghayiteyuga poem, published in the outline pamphlet of 2017 BS. Poems in this stream are mainly marked by an abstract writing style, incommunicability, structural looseness, new images, the use of symbols and myths, presentation of the absurd, and existential consciousness. Basing itself on these, the theme, plot, character, setting, purpose, and language style of Narasimha Avatar are studied and analysed. It is clear from this study that this epic has turned into something experimental with a new form — rather than the conventional epic structure — in its selection of subject matter, building of the plot, characterisation, creation of setting, and use of language style alongside its purpose.
informal_english: This piece takes a look at Jagadish Shamsher Rana's epic Narasimha Avatar through a pragmatist lens. Now, pragmatism isn't really an 'ism' at all — it's just what folks call it when literature tries something new. In Nepali poetry, pragmatism refers to that new poetry wave that kicked off with Mohan Koirala's Ghayiteyuga poem, which came out in the 2017 BS outline pamphlet. The poems in that wave are mostly about abstract writing, being hard to get across, loose structure, fresh images, symbols and myths, the absurd, and existential vibes. Using those as a jumping-off point, this study looks at the theme, plot, characters, setting, purpose, and language of Narasimha Avatar. The upshot is clear: this epic's gone off and done its own thing with a new form instead of sticking to the old-school epic structure — whether that's picking the subject, shaping the plot, drawing the characters, setting the scene, or the language it uses.
translator_notes: Year 2017 BS (Bikram Sambat) preserved as in source; Nepali term पि.सं./वि.सं. rendered as BS. No missing ending detected in abstract.
